subject: Support for November Ballot Questions
overview: The Committee voted to formally support several November ballot initiatives, including the elimination of MCAS as a graduation requirement and local tax overrides for city and school operations. Members also approved the City Year partnership funding and a new senior parking spot decoration program.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: The Committee entered executive session to discuss contract negotiations and strategy for non-union personnel and various director and principal positions.

items.title: Superintendent's Report
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent provided updates on curriculum nights, the high school building project, ongoing bus transportation shortages, and upcoming community events like Run Medford.

items.title: City Year Budget Transfer
items.summary: Approved a $200,000 budget transfer to fund the City Year partnership, with expenses split between the school budget and the before-and-after school revolving fund.

items.title: Cummings Foundation and Project Transition Donations
items.summary: Approved a $10,000 grant from the Cummings Foundation for arts enrichment and an anonymous $1,000 donation to support the Project Transition vocational program.

items.title: City Year Partnership Update
items.summary: Representatives from City Year and the McGlynn Middle School Principal presented on the integration of AmeriCorps members into classrooms for academic and social-emotional support.

items.title: Senior Parking Spot Painting Fee
items.summary: Approved a $75 fee for seniors to paint and decorate their own parking spots as a class fundraiser, while a proposed general $75 parking fee for all students was not moved for a vote.

items.title: Policy AC: Non-Discrimination
items.summary: Approved the second reading of updated non-discrimination policies to align with new federal Title IX regulations.

items.title: Resolution on November 2024 Ballot Questions
items.summary: Approved resolutions supporting state Question 2 regarding MCAS graduation requirements and local Questions 7 and 8 concerning tax overrides for city and school funding.

items.title: Tobacco and Nicotine Policy
items.summary: Approved the first reading of an updated policy prohibiting tobacco and nicotine products on school premises, including an amendment to specifically list nicotine pouches.

items.title: Facilities Maintenance Consolidation
items.summary: Approved language defining the city facilities director's role in supporting school maintenance, procurement, and preventative maintenance tasks.
